replies.author: luuk0987
replies.body: I've been using comfyUI but it's been hit or miss mostly. Any tips for models/prompts?

replies.author: EchoAIAgent
replies.body:
First I give Claude the concept art. For characters that’s a turnaround sheet: front, side and back views on one image.  
Then I ask it to cut up the sheet and write the workflow. Here I give Claude control of my PC to save the files straight into ComfyUI's folders  
I tell Claude to check what boxes and settings exist and make sure that the workflow uses the most optimal for the character

A prompt for this could be  
"Here’s my character turnaround sheet. Crop it into front, side and back views, and write a ComfyUI workflow that turns them into a textured 3D model with Tripo, under 15,000 polygons. Save it to my workflows folder and check it against my running ComfyUI before I run it. Tell me how many paid generations it will use."

comments.author: ArcaneMoose
comments.body: Love the look and feel! What is the "art style" of this and how did you get it looking consistent? What did you ask for to get the textures like that? Any prompt tips to get a similar art style?

replies.author: EchoAIAgent
replies.body:
The trick to get a consistent artstyle is to focus more on rendering and light. My objective was to make them have a soft art toy look, almost clay-like without fully reaching the uneven plasticine look of claymation, so that's what I asked ChatGPT to make as concepts. I explained my idea for the game and the concept of the characters as chibi-esque humanoid critters that had entheogenic plants as the main motif and then I gave it the rendering style and material guides.  
**Giving a motif to base the designs around is very important.**  
Once the first results came in and I was satisfied with it, I asked it to make a design bible that will be what every other design will need to be based around. World, foliage, enemies, shaders. Everything must adhere to this design language.

replies.author: EchoAIAgent
replies.body: For animation I used the Kimodo plugin in Unreal Engine. It was a matter of describing how I wanted it to look like and then tweaking the animations generated with a back and forth with Claude, descriptions like "Make the head bobble more", "try to have erratic movements around the arms and head", "Incline their bodies to make it feel like their heavy heads can't keep up with the rest of their body". Simple stuff like that.

They can!  
You can do it through ComfyUI or through their platform.  
I simply asked Claude to use ComfyUI to make the reference images with a Nano Banana workflow. For some reason the gens from Nano Banana worked better than the ones made with GPT Image. No idea why though.

replies.author: RemarkableWish2508
replies.body:
GPT Image still has an annoying mini-grid super-detail tendency that adds effectively high-frequency noise to images (more obvious in some than others).

Nano Banana does things somehow differently, and while neither is pure diffusion, its outputs are easier for other models (or itself) to extract what's going on in them.
